cities.name: Shillong
cities.overview: Meghalaya's hill capital, once called the 'Scotland of the East', with pine forests, colonial bungalows, busy markets and a famous live-music scene.
cities.history: The British made Shillong the capital of Assam in 1874, and it stayed so until Meghalaya was formed in 1972. Pine trees and colonial houses earned it the name Scotland of the East.

cities.name: Sohra
cities.overview: Sohra (Cherrapunji) sits on a plateau in the East Khasi Hills, about 55 km from Shillong. It is one of the wettest places on earth, surrounded by waterfalls, gorges, caves and living root bridges.

cities.name: Mawlynnong
cities.overview: A small Khasi village near the Bangladesh border, famous for its cleanliness, flower-lined paths and community-run tourism.

cities.name: Dawki
cities.overview: A border town in the West Jaintia Hills on the Umngot River, a trade crossing with Bangladesh known for its remarkably clear water.

cities.name: Jowai
cities.overview: The main town of the Jaintia Hills, known for its Behdienkhlam festival and the monoliths at Nartiang.

cities.name: Tura
cities.overview: The main town of the Garo Hills, in the far west of the state.

cities.name: Mawphlang
cities.overview: A Khasi village 25 km from Shillong, known for its sacred grove.

places.name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge
places.shortDescription: A two-level bridge grown from the roots of rubber fig trees, reached by a steep trek down to Nongriat village.
places.description: From Tyrna village, about 3,500 steps drop through the forest to Nongriat, crossing swaying wire bridges over turquoise streams. At the bottom is the Umshiang Double Decker Root Bridge, with two tiers of living roots trained across a stream, and natural pools for swimming. The climb back up is tough; start early, carry water, or stay overnight in a Nongriat homestay. Rainbow Falls is a further hour's walk.
places.history: Khasi and Jaintia communities have grown root bridges for generations by guiding the aerial roots of Ficus elastica trees across rivers until they strengthen into bridges that can last for centuries. The living root bridges of Meghalaya were added to UNESCO's Tentative List in 2022.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March for safer trails; the monsoon is dramatic but slippery.

entryFee.note: Small village entry and camera fees are collected along the route.

timings.hours: Start the trek by morning; allow 4–6 hours round trip

location.address: Nongriat village, near Tyrna, East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya 793108

images.alt: Double Decker Living Root Bridge, Sohra

places.name: Nohkalikai Falls
places.shortDescription: India's tallest plunge waterfall, dropping about 340 metres into a green pool below the Sohra plateau.
places.description: Nohkalikai Falls drops in a single plunge off the plateau edge, fed by rain collected on the tableland above. A viewing area at the top gives the classic view, and on a clear day you can see the vivid green pool far below. For the adventurous, a steep trail leads down to the pool. Mist can hide the falls entirely during the monsoon, so be prepared to wait for it to clear.
places.history: The falls are named after a Khasi legend about a grief-stricken woman, Ka Likai, who leapt from the cliff.
places.bestTimeNote: June to September for the strongest flow; October–November for clearer views.

location.address: Nohkalikai, Sohra, East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya 793108

places.name: Mawsmai Cave
places.shortDescription: A lit limestone cave near Sohra where visitors squeeze through narrow passages among stalactites.
places.description: Mawsmai is the most accessible of Meghalaya's many limestone caves. A route of about 150 metres is lit, with some narrow, low sections where you have to crouch or squeeze through. Stalactites, stalagmites and fossil-like formations line the walls. It is a short, fun stop between the waterfalls of Sohra.

location.address: Mawsmai village, Sohra, East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya 793108

places.name: Mawlynnong Village
places.shortDescription: A spotless Khasi village with bamboo dustbins, orchid gardens and a tree-top 'sky walk' over the Bangladesh plains.
places.description: Mawlynnong's residents share the work of keeping the village clean, and bamboo dustbins stand along its stone paths. Climb the bamboo sky walk for views towards Bangladesh, visit the small church, and walk to the Riwai living root bridge nearby. Several families run homestays serving local Khasi food.
places.history: In 2003 a travel magazine named Mawlynnong the 'cleanest village in Asia', and the community has built tourism around that reputation ever since.

entryFee.note: Small village fee; the sky walk and root bridge charge separately.

places.name: Umngot River, Dawki
places.shortDescription: A river so clear in winter that boats appear to float in mid-air above the riverbed.
places.description: In the dry season the Umngot is clear enough to see the pebbles several metres below the boats. Hire a wooden boat at Dawki or the nearby village of Shnongpdeng, where you can also go snorkelling, cliff-jumping, kayaking and camping on the riverbank. The suspension bridge over the river dates from the British era.
places.bestTimeNote: November to April, when the water is clearest. Monsoon rains make it muddy.

entryFee.note: Boat rides are priced per boat; activities at Shnongpdeng are extra.

timings.hours: Boating from morning to about 4:00 PM

places.name: Umiam Lake
places.shortDescription: A large reservoir framed by pine-covered hills on the road into Shillong, with water sports and viewpoints.
places.description: Umiam Lake (Barapani) is the first big view visitors see on the drive from Guwahati to Shillong. The water-sports complex offers kayaking, speed boats and water scooters, and lakeside resorts and viewpoints are good for sunset. Cycling and camping are popular around the shore.
places.history: The lake was created in the early 1960s by damming the Umiam River for hydroelectric power.

places.name: Laitlum Canyons
places.shortDescription: Grassy ridges that end in sheer drops over deep green gorges, an hour from Shillong.
places.description: Laitlum means 'end of the hills', and the ridge here drops away into deep valleys with views that stretch for miles on a clear day. Walk along the edge for photographs, or take the long stone stairway down to the village of Rasong in the valley below. Mist often rolls in through the gorges in the afternoon, so come early.

entryFee.note: Small entry and parking fees collected by the village.

location.address: Laitlum, Smit, East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya 793015

places.name: Elephant Falls
places.shortDescription: A two-tier waterfall on the edge of Shillong, named after an elephant-shaped rock.
places.description: A short stair leads to viewpoints of each tier in the forest, with the fullest flow after the monsoon. The rock itself collapsed in an 1897 earthquake.

places.name: Ward's Lake
places.shortDescription: A horseshoe-shaped garden lake in the middle of Shillong, from British days.
places.description: An ornamental lake with a wooden bridge and boating, right at the centre of town. It's a favourite spot for an evening stroll.

places.name: Shillong Peak
places.shortDescription: The highest point in the Khasi Hills, with a sweeping view of Shillong from an air force area.
places.description: A short drive leads up through a military area, with a viewing deck over the city. You may need to show ID at the gate.

places.name: Mawphlang Sacred Grove
places.shortDescription: An ancient sacred forest of the Khasi people, where nothing may be removed, 25 km from Shillong.
places.description: Guided walks explain the Khasi beliefs and monoliths in a forest that's been protected for centuries by tradition.

places.name: Nartiang Durga Temple
places.shortDescription: A Hindu shrine in the Jaintia Hills, near the tallest monoliths in the Khasi and Jaintia country.
places.description: Close to a hilltop garden of tall standing stones, the Nartiang temple is among the Shakti Peethas, and it's linked to the Jaintia kings.

places.name: Siju Cave
places.shortDescription: A long limestone cave in the South Garo Hills, one of the most significant in India, full of bats.
places.description: Beside the Simsang River, this big cave is known for its bats and its stream passage. Bring a guide and expect to wade.

places.name: Nokrek National Park
places.shortDescription: A biosphere reserve around the highest Garo peak, with red pandas and a rare citrus.
places.description: Forest around Nokrek Peak, with a remarkable gene pool of wild citrus and a reputation for red pandas and hoolock gibbons.

places.name: Balpakram National Park
places.shortDescription: A remote Garo Hills park, with a huge canyon sacred to the Garo people as a home of spirits.
places.description: A high plateau and deep gorge near the Bangladesh border, sometimes called the Grand Canyon of Meghalaya. It's little visited.

places.name: Nongriat Village
places.shortDescription: A Khasi village in a deep valley, known for the double-decker living root bridge and blue pools.
places.description: You reach it by thousands of steps down from Tyrna, passing wire and root bridges. Homestays let you stay overnight in the valley.
